title: Schedule, with room to read
lede: Clearer event rows and a calmer Event detail screen, shown at standard text size.

stats.n: Gotham Black becomes Gotham Bold. Dates, location, and crew stay directly below.

sections.heading: Schedule and Event detail
sections.note: Matched iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 26.5 captures with the same fixture data, light appearance, standard text size, and top scroll position. CSS excludes the changing status-bar clock; original screenshots are preserved.

pairs.title: Schedule: venue and coverage get breathing room
pairs.beforeCap: Venue text shrinks to share a line with crew coverage.
pairs.afterCap: Long venues keep their text size; coverage moves below when needed.

pairs.title: Event detail: identity first, quieter controls
pairs.beforeCap: Heavy headline and repeated red outlined crew menus.
pairs.afterCap: Lighter headline, neutral toolbar actions, and simple gray crew menus.

pairs.title: Multi-day event: one readable date range
pairs.beforeCap: The date and countdown are separate competing text elements.
pairs.afterCap: A wrapping date line keeps the full event span together.

changes.was: Titles, venues, and personal-work text had tight line limits or shrinking.
changes.now: Rows grow where needed, keeping the same time, venue classification, crew counts, and personal assignment context.

changes.was: Each assigned crew member had a red outlined overflow icon.
changes.now: A quiet ellipsis keeps the same menu and 44 pt touch target. The event’s main action retains its prominent treatment.

verification: Wisconsin builds and standard Schedule/Event detail screenshot tests pass on iPhone 16 Pro. List, Calendar, ended, live, and all-day detail screens are captured.
Xcode project consistency, iOS drift, audit coverage, docs verification, and diff checks pass.
One broader temporal-state test has a pre-existing literal assertion for the old working-copy assignment expression; committed HEAD uses the guarded intermediate value.
notes: Local UI implementation only; no commit, push, or TestFlight release.
The published-crew warning is an existing fixture fallback caused by an unmapped working-copy request. The same state is present in both columns; this is not a production incident.
Availability, Trade Board, and staff editing screens are outside this pass.
